definitions.gloss: medicinal effect; therapeutic efficacy; pharmaceutical effect
definitions.explanation: The healing or therapeutic effect of a medicine, herb, or substance. Refers to how well a drug or remedy works to treat a condition.

examples.english: It has a strong medicinal effect.

examples.japanese: この{温泉|おんせん}には{薬効|やっこう}があると{言|い}われている。
examples.english: This hot spring is said to have therapeutic effects.

examples.japanese: {漢方薬|かんぽうやく}は{西洋|せいよう}{医学|いがく}とは{異|こと}なる{薬効|やっこう}の{考|かんが}え{方|かた}に{基|もと}づいている。
examples.english: Traditional Chinese medicine is based on a different way of thinking about medicinal effects than Western medicine.

notes:
A compound of {薬|やく} (medicine) and {効|こう} (effect, efficacy). Used in medical, pharmaceutical, and traditional medicine contexts. Also commonly appears in descriptions of hot springs ({温泉|おんせん}), herbs, and health foods.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {薬効|やっこう}がある: to have a medicinal effect
- {薬効|やっこう}が{高|たか}い: to have a strong medicinal effect
- {薬効|やっこう}{成分|せいぶん}: active pharmaceutical ingredient
- {薬効|やっこう}を{示|しめ}す: to show therapeutic efficacy
- {温泉|おんせん}の{薬効|やっこう}: therapeutic effects of hot springs

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {効能|こうのう}: efficacy, virtue — often used for hot springs and traditional remedies
- {効果|こうか}: effect, result — a more general term not limited to medicine
- {副作用|ふくさよう}: side effect — unintended effects of medicine, as opposed to the intended {薬効|やっこう}
